question: In the DX-Scorecard MBR multi-screen redesign (Reviews entry then collection then builder then Preview), what hash-route structure should be used given App.tsx/useHashRoute currently expose only a single #mbr route, and how do the Continue-to-builder, Cancel, Discard, Preview, and back-out transitions map onto those routes?
recommendation: Keep a single 'mbr' RouteView but namespace the four screens as segmented sub-routes under the #mbr prefix, parsed exactly like the existing #locked/<id> pattern: #mbr (Reviews entry/list) → #mbr/collect (collection) → #mbr/build (builder) → #mbr/preview (Preview). Extend parseHash so head 'mbr' reads rest[0] into a new `step` field (defaulting to the Reviews entry when absent), and have App keep dispatching the whole family to the DEV-gated MbrBuilderView, which switches on route.step. Map the transitions as: Continue-to-builder navigates #mbr/collect → #mbr/build; Preview navigates #mbr/build → #mbr/preview; back-out from Preview returns #mbr/preview → #mbr/build; Cancel (from collection) returns to the Reviews entry #mbr; and Discard (from builder, after its confirm modal) also returns to the Reviews entry #mbr.
supporting_points: The codebase already has a working precedent: parseHash splits the hash on '/' into [head, ...rest] and #locked/<id> yields { view: 'locked', id }. Reusing head='mbr' with rest[0] as a `step` keeps one RouteView, so App.tsx's production dead-code guard (the `route.view === 'mbr'` check that tree-shakes the builder out of the prod bundle per ADR-003) and useHashRoute's KNOWN_VIEWS stay untouched — no new top-level views to gate or strip.

Sub-path segments (#mbr/collect, #mbr/build, #mbr/preview) rather than sibling top-level hashes (#mbrcollect, #mbrbuild) preserve the flow's ownership and make transitions plain window.location.hash assignments; bare #mbr sensibly defaults to the Reviews entry, matching how bare #locked already falls back gracefully. Cancel and Discard both unwind to that entry (#mbr), while Preview↔builder is a reversible hop between #mbr/build and #mbr/preview, giving natural browser Back behaviour.

This structure cleanly layers onto the existing MbrBuilderView state machine: its Discard already runs through a confirm modal before re-seeding, so routing Discard back to #mbr on confirm fits; Continue-to-builder maps to the collection→builder step; and Preview is a new read-only render of the same working draft, so keeping it under #mbr/preview (same view module, same DEV gate) avoids duplicating the draft-load/persist wiring across separate routes.
